newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras calls out the troops to stop crime wave.
newsitem.headline: Honduras calls out the troops to stop crime wave.

text.p: Thousands of army troops were deployed on city streets throughout Honduras on Friday to help the government fight a growing crime wave, military officials said.
Army officials said 2,000 troops hit the streets of eight cities as part of a stepped-up government effort to curb violent crime.
"By deploying troops on the streets, we aim to protect the public from this crime wave that has gripped our country," said Col. Rodolfo Interiano, commander of the country's First Infantry Batallion.
Officials said the military operations were code-named "Operation Leopard" in the capital Tegucigalpa and "Operation Panther" in Honduras' second city of San Pedro Sula.
Officials say bank robberies, kidnapping, muggings and other crimes are becoming more commonplace in Honduras, one of the poorest countries in the Western Hemisphere.
The deployment comes amid increasing calls by the military for an increase in its budget. Military leaders want their 1997 buget nearly doubled, although lawmakers have so far refused their request.
